facts.claim: Sunbelt Rentals' Spring Valley NY branch (12.5 miles from Peekskill) rents a 12-inch, 85 HP diesel chipper for $430 a day, $1,450 a week and $3,525 for four weeks, pickup.

source.name: Sunbelt Rentals — 12 Inch Wood Chipper (live rate card, Spring Valley NY branch #785, pickup)

facts.caveat: Online rate for the dates 9/21–9/22/2026. Rates vary by branch and date.

topics.title: New York: subcontractor or employee
topics.summary: How the state decides. The facts of the relationship control, not the label.

facts.claim: The NY Department of Labor looks at the degree of supervision, direction and control. No single factor decides it. Being told when, where and how to work and being paid hourly points to employee; being in business for yourself and serving the public points to independent contractor.

source.name: NYS Department of Labor — Independent Contractors

facts.claim: Per NY DOL, designating a worker an independent contractor, even with the worker's agreement and a written contract, does not make it so. The facts of the relationship are still examined.

source.name: NYS Department of Labor — Independent Contractors

facts.claim: For most industries the Workers' Compensation Board weighs about ten factors, including control, a separately established business, carrying liability insurance, providing your own equipment, and signs of an independent business such as advertising, an FEIN and permits.

source.name: NYS Workers' Compensation Board — Identifying an Independent Contractor

facts.caveat: Page is undated. Working with the other company's equipment weighs toward employee.

facts.claim: Under the Construction Industry Fair Play Act (effective October 26, 2010) an individual is an independent contractor only if all three conditions are met, and a separate business entity must meet all twelve criteria.

source.name: NYS Workers' Compensation Board — Identifying an Independent Contractor

facts.claim: We have not determined whether tree work counts as 'construction' under the Fair Play Act. The DOL web page does not define the term; fact sheet P738 may.

source.name: NYS Department of Labor — Construction Industry Fair Play Act

facts.caveat: Question for an accountant or attorney.

topics.title: New York: workers comp and subcontractors
topics.summary: What happens at audit when a sub has no comp policy, and what paper counts.

facts.claim: NYSIF: if a subcontractor has no workers comp coverage, the sub is included in the hiring company's policy, and the hiring company is responsible for the premium and for claims.

source.name: New York State Insurance Fund — Subcontractor Coverage

facts.claim: NYSIF asks for every subcontractor's certificate of insurance at premium audit. If they can't be produced, premium is recalculated with those subs counted as payroll. NYSIF-covered subs can be checked with NYSIF's Certificate Validation tool; others with the WCB Employer Coverage Search.

source.name: New York State Insurance Fund — Subcontractor Coverage

facts.claim: Form CE-200 (Certificate of Attestation of Exemption) is only for government permits, licenses and contracts. The WCB states it cannot be used to show another business, or that business's insurance carrier, that coverage is not required.

source.name: NYS Workers' Compensation Board — Certificate of Attestation of Exemption (CE-200)

facts.caveat: What a carrier will accept from a one-person sub with no comp policy is a question for the carrier, before the first job.

topics.title: Who may run the iron
topics.summary: Operator and driver rules that apply under any arrangement.

facts.claim: OSHA: only trained and authorized persons may operate an aerial lift. The employer is responsible for instructing employees in recognizing and avoiding unsafe conditions (29 CFR 1926.21(b)(2)).

source.name: OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.453 Aerial lifts, and Aerial Lifts fact sheet

facts.caveat: 1926 is the construction standard. Tree care may fall under general-industry rule 1910.67, not yet read.

facts.claim: In New York a single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more requires a commercial driver license; Class B covers a single-unit truck.

source.name: NY DMV — Driver license class descriptions

facts.caveat: Check the GVWR on each truck's door sticker.

topics.title: How rental pricing works
topics.summary: How yards build day, week and month rates, what a 'day' means, and what the sticker price leaves out.

facts.claim: On four machines at one Sunbelt branch, a week costs 2.2 to 3.4 times the day rate and four weeks costs 5.0 to 8.2 times the day rate.

source.name: Sunbelt Rentals — site search results priced for Spring Valley NY branch #785

facts.caveat: One company, one branch, one day. Online claims of 10–12x daily had no vendor data behind them.

facts.claim: Sunbelt defines One Shift as not more than 8 hours a day, 40 hours a week and 160 hours per four weeks on the hour meter. Double shift is billed at 150% and triple shift at 200%.

source.name: Sunbelt Rentals — US Terms & Conditions

facts.claim: Sunbelt requires business renters to carry at least $1,000,000 per-occurrence general liability plus all-risk property insurance on the equipment for its fair market value, naming Sunbelt as additional insured and loss payee, primary and non-contributory, with waiver of subrogation. Insurance that excludes boom damage or overturns is a breach.

source.name: Sunbelt Rentals — US Terms & Conditions

facts.claim: Sunbelt's Rental Protection Plan costs 15% of gross rental charges. It is not insurance and does not cover liability to others. It caps the renter's bill for accidental damage or loss at 10% of the cost, up to $500 per piece.

source.name: Sunbelt Rentals — Rental Protection Plan

facts.caveat: Sunbelt's own examples: theft of a $96,200 machine costs the renter $500 with the plan; $2,000 of minor accidental damage costs $200. Exclusions include intentional misuse and unreported theft.

facts.claim: At Sunbelt the renter replaces the fuel (prepay, pay on return, or return full), and an environmental fee is added as a percentage of the rental.

source.name: Sunbelt Rentals — Fees & Optional Charges
